purpose: Keyword table the Retell agent prompt can embed to map a spoken free-text answer onto the 1-5 agreement scale, onto one of three options, onto the 1-5 energy scale (working genius), onto the 1-6 similarity scale (values), or onto a clock time (chronotype). Mirrors parseScaleAnswer / parseOptionAnswer / parseEnergyAnswer / parseSimilarityAnswer / parseClockAnswer in scoring.ts.
rules: A spoken number (1-5, or 'x out of 5', 'x out of 10') beats any keyword.
Otherwise take the longest matching phrase; if several match with equal length, take the one that appears last (people correct themselves: 'yeah... actually not really' -> 2).
Negation: 'not' directly before a 5-word maps to 2 ('not completely' -> 2); 'not' before a 4-word maps to 2. 'not at all' and 'not really' are already whole phrases and win as phrases.
If nothing matches, do not guess. Re-ask with the scale: 'Would you say not at all, a little, somewhat, mostly, or completely?'
A long story answer: pick the phrase that best summarizes the stance, confirm it in five words or fewer ('So, mostly?'), then move on. Never read the item again in full.

three_option.by_content: If no letter or position is given, match the answer to the option whose words overlap most (e.g. 'I'd just wing it' -> the option containing 'wing it'). If overlap is weak or tied, confirm: 'So closer to A, B, or C?'
three_option.neither: If the person says 'none of those' or 'between A and B', record the respond-zone option when one of the two is respond; otherwise record the one they lean toward and flag `uncertain: true`.

energy_1_5.used_by: working_genius energy items. Numbers 1-5 win, then these phrases (longest match, last occurrence), then fall back to scale_1_5 ('yeah' -> 4, 'not at all' -> 1).

similarity_1_6.used_by: values items. Numbers 1-6 win ('x out of 10' -> ceil(x * 6 / 10)), then these phrases (longest match, last occurrence). 'like me' alone is 5; the longer phrases around it ('not like me', 'a little like me') win because they are longer.
similarity_1_6.rule: If nothing matches, re-ask with the six labels. Never collapse this to the 1-5 table.

clock.used_by: chronotype K_wake and K_bed. Record the time as said ('6:30', 'half past seven', '11 pm', 'midnight'); the scorer parses it.
rules: Pass the spoken time through verbatim; do not convert.
A bare number with no a.m./p.m. is read as morning for the wake item, and for the bed item as evening when 7-12 and after midnight when 1-6.
If the person gives a range ('six or seven'), ask for the one that's most typical and record that.
If they say 'it depends' or give a day-of-week answer, ask for the free day with no alarm.
